steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Titi...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Fetch!

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: (Fetches the ball)

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: (Brings it back)

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Who's the cutest little thing? You are!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Stop fooling around, Titi!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I've always wanted a pet, but my family wouldn't let me have one. Look how cute it is!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It's not a pet, its part of the museum's collection.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Tell that to Pepe. She's yelling at part of the museum's collection.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: SAY THAT AGAIN?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I apologize, Pepe Khanum, but I am unable to answer. My memories of the trove's location remain vague.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You sure you don't want to stop her? I'm starting to feel sorry for that corpse cowering in a corner.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well, try harder! Maybe you'll remember then.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I'm afraid that would be futile...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: They who split my memories distributed them evenly across all the gems, to ensure that the secret could not be easily accessed.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: There are five gems in total. You may have to find all of them before I can tell you the answer.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Where are the rest of the gems? You must know that, right?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You don't?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: The army that defeated me consisted of many padishahs and lords ameer... They took the gems with them when they left.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's like looking for a needle in a haystack...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: There must be another way! Use that golden brain of yours!
Zubayr is forced into a corner by Pepe, even as the short girl doesn't come up to his chest.
He feels a pressure so great, it threatens to buckle even his hardened metal kneecaps.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Please, hanimefendi... have patience...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Then tell me something useful!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: There is a faint resonance between the gems that I can sense if I am in their proximity.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Are you kidding me? You want me to take you across all of Sargon? This city alone holds thousands of gems!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I think I sense one faintly...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well, what are we waiting for? Let's go!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Look, Anat, she's trying to remove part of the museum's collection!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Pepe, Zubayr Effendi is a valued part of the museum's collection. We must ensure that he is stored under appropriate conditions, and I can't allow him to be exposed to the elements.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Leave that thought and do your research here. Do NOT go out.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Forty-percent increase in funding next year?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Double?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: My staff will be watching you at all times. Senebty.

spans.text: My staff will be watching you at all times.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What's come over her?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Zubayr Effendi, I know it's not exactly polite to ask a man for his funeral effects, but I would be remiss...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Can I borrow this for a couple of days?

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: (Spins rapidly)

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Of course, hanimefendi.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You can come out now, Zubayr. There's no one here.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: How do you go through a hole like that at your size? It's like you turned liquid or something.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: My body is extremely flexible, allowing me to pass through narrow spaces.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I thought I would have to tear down the wall, if you couldn't get out.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: There is no need.
Zubayr closes his eyes and shakes his sistrum.
As the chimes ring, the wall around the hole slowly turns to sand, falling to the ground, leaving behind a much bigger hole.
With eyes wide, Pepe walks back and forth through the hole, then picks up a handful of sand.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Why didn't you use your Originium Arts? I almost hit my head crawling through the hole.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You didn't ask.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well... you should close it back up. Wouldn't want anyone else to see it.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: As you wish.
The chimes ring again, and sand flows back into the hole. Soon, there is no sign that the hole was ever there.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Centuries ago, there was nothing but sand. Now, tall buildings line the streets. Such prosperity.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Lamps line the banks of the river flowing gently through the city. It reminds me of Shar-Cheshmeh, built upon an oasis.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Shahr-Cheshmeh, the City of Springs? I thought it was just a legend. No one has found it in centuries.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: No, it was very real. Its padishah was a despot who challenged the Shah's authority on multiple occasions. I had to pay him a personal visit.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: And then?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: And then it was no more.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Did... the whole city have to pay for the sins of a single padishah?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I did nothing but cut the padishah's head off and throw it into a spring. It was the chained slaves who burned the city to the ground.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: If you visited yourself, you would be shocked by the filth and stink. They made sacrifices in the water, but the water system was... primitive.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Please, stop. I can almost smell it.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I see. Can we go to the river?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No, not that way!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's early. The banks of the river are still brightly lit. Anat would kill me if someone saw the museum's collection walking the streets.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I know a place. Follow me.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Curator Anat, we've taken inventory of the collection. Here it is...

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: ...Medjehtiqedti Khanum? What are you doing here?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Anat went to meet a guest, so I'm taking over some of the documents.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: 'The Padishah's statue wasn't damaged in an accident; it was missing one eyeball to begin with! Who wrote this?'

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Ha...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: How's my impression?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: But it's true that the statue's records are wrong. Be careful next time.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: R-Really? Let me see who was in charge.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Izaja and Inaja. I think they were under your...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Ahem... here, Age of Shadow exhibits counted twice. Make sure you double-check.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: This is...?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: My favorite place in the city.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You like empty streets.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's not like this during the day. Everything in Menat-Ha'mait goes through here.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Merchants from all across the country come here to trade gems, furs, spices, crafts... people come from other countries too, often making large transactions.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: If we're going to find a gem somewhere, this would be it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Deep in the Grand Bazaar is a trading post dedicated to gems. Virtually every gem in the city passes through it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Do you sense the gem we're looking for?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Are you listening?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Forgive me...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I am curious about the crafts being sold here. In my time, animal sculptures like these were guardians of tombs, companions for the dead.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Now, though, they are being peddled on the streets as everyday items.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well... it's a decorative sculpture for home use. Twenty-five dinars.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: From the murals on the walls, to the hieroglyphs all around... many things feel so familiar, yet so strange at the same time.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Perhaps we should go and see a few more places?

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Medjehtiqedti Hanimefendi, the great families have sent inquiries.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: The padishahs take the solemnity of Sargonian history so seriously. How do we explain this incident to them?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Just tell them it was an intern's mistake and we'll deal with it accordingly.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Deal with whom?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: The acting curator, perhaps?

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Is it really true, Titi?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: There was unexplained access made using your pass both last night and this morning... what if someone investigates?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: That can't be! I wiped all the records clean.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: So you've finally admitted it.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I didn't... I...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Well, this I can cover up... but the mummy coming back to life, on the eve of the Flood Festival, is another matter.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: What's your plan?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: To keep the museum closed until things blow over.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: No way!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Look at that badgir!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: A windcatcher, yes, the most common type of tower here. Those openings catch the cool, high winds and guide them into the building through vents.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Cool air flows into the space below, pushing the hot air out the opposite side.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I didn't know you were an architect.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I'm not. But I met the talented architect who invented the badgir.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Do you sense the gems yet?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I'm sorry... I can't sense any nearby. Maybe I could tell you something else.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Are you not curious how the gems retain one's memory and consciousness?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I AM curious. I figured it was some kind of Sarkaz witchcraft related to the Zhayedan.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: People in my time believed that life consists of three parts: Body, Name, and Soul.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Body is the physical vessel, and Name is the identity known to others. The Soul, however, is what truly makes us human; it is the emotions and experiences that form our character.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: All three parts must be preserved together, in order for life to be eternal.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: The Body can be replaced with something more durable. The Name can retain its meaning by being passed on through generations.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I know. That's the genesis of Sargonian noble heritage.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: The Soul, however, is the frailest of the three.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: During the Age of Shadow, it was discovered that part of the Soul can be preserved, in a manner of speaking, by etching it upon a pure gem with Originium circuits.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Like the gem in your chest...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I've only ever read about it in ancient texts... Scholars call it superstition, borne out of a lack of understanding of the nature of life.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: That is a misinterpretation.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: However, the true mystery, the method by which a life's journey is engraved, has long since been lost to time.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Or, it might exist, to some degree... gems with engraved Originium circuits can still be found in this city.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Last year, a gem with Originium circuits that could change the ambient temperature in a small area was sold at auction for an incredible price.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Some things survive the test of time, only to become barely recognizable.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The sun's about to rise. We should get back before the museum opens. Let's go.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The museum is just ahead. I don't want to crawl through another hole. Why don't we use your Arts to make a shortcut?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: One moment, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Have you sensed the gem?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I would like to see the sunrise.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: The one thing that the passage of time cannot change.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Okay. Just for a bit.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: How lucky. It is still bright, glorious, brilliant.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: It still brings warmth.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Inudi harek, Horakhet.
Zubayr slumbered for centuries beneath the sands, with only darkness for company.
He squints straight at the sun rising in the east, the brilliant wheel of flame.
Sunlight shines upon him for the first time in a very long while, illuminating his golden body.
Pepe can barely open her eyes, so bright it is.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Is it time to go back?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You can stay a while longer, if you like being in the sun.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: We have a little bit of time.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: The sun is up.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Four days... no, five, since Narantuya went missing.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Focus, Ajazi! This work requires attention to detail!

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: You're sure that the communicator fell into this drainage outlet when we left the museum, right?

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: I'm sure.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Well, we've been dredging through it every day, but we haven't found a shadow of it.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: We can't reach Narantuya if we don't find it. if we can't reach Narantuya... what will we do?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: ...I remember Narantuya saying we should find a way to get money when she's not around.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: You're right, Ajani!

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: We need to pull a big job.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: That way, we can buy a new communicator and get in touch with the boss!

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Let's go. We've got work to do at the museum.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Hey, Ajazi, I think I hooked something!

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: What do you think, Lazvar?

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: A hue like the night sky, and the wavy patterns it like lava gently flowing across it...

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: It was dug up from the deep Obsidian veins decades ago. It's a rare treasure today, given the state of Mount Siesta.

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: The gem vendors in town dare not give a hasty quote for it, and you've been away from the post these past few days...

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: There is no Originium circuit on this gem.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: I'm afraid I cannot give you a high price for it.
The blue fowlbeast that was perched on the overseer's staff flies up, grabs the Obsidian, and places it gently on the scale.
The scale comes to a halt, and the young overseer looks at the reading.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Three hundred and seventy dinars.

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: B-But a Siestan collector offered a much higher price for it! The equivalent of thirty-seven thousand dinars!

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: Could you perhaps be mistaken?

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: You could always go back to that collector.

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: Ah, er, well, it's not that I don't trust the overseer's eyes and scales...

steps.name: Eager Woman
steps.text: But if we were in Londinium, Lungmen, or Siesta...

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: We're in Menat-Ha'mait.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: There are treasures here beyond reckoning. The sand beneath your feet was perhaps at one time gems brighter than the stars.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: That is why we value the power of a gem far more than its appearance.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Three hundred and seventy dinars is the most I can give for an ordinary Obsidian, with no Originium circuits or special powers.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Can we really sell a rock that we reeled in from the sewers?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Even the roads in this city are paved with gems. Try holding it under the sun.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: What am I supposed to see?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Nothing. It's like the plastic handle of my toothbrush.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Well, don't be discouraged, Ajani. It could help Narantuya's great endeavor, even if it's not worth much.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Like, she could enjoy ice water for an entire week once she comes back. Added with lemon slices and dried dates for sure.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Hey, you! Yeah, you, behind the counter.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Yeah. You're the receptionist, right?

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Receptionist? No—

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: It's our first time here. We want to... to... what do we want to do, Ajazi?

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: To get this gem appraised and sell it for good money!

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Yeah, that's right. Do you know where the queue for gem appraisals is?

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: ...Give it to me. I can appraise it.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Wow, even the receptionist at the gem trading post knows how to appraise gems!

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: At first glance, it is a pale sapphire of low-purity.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Low-purity? Sounds like dried dates are off the menu.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Well, the lemon slices still have a chance.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: The Originium circuits are clearly visible. Hm? This is...

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: What is it? Is there something wrong with the circuits?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Meh, never mind, Ajazi. The gem probably doesn't do anything, judging by his reaction.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: ...No, it does. The Originium circuits on this gem can induce excitement in small animals.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: It makes small animals excited...?

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Where are you going, Ajani?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Back to work at the museum, of course! You know how much money we're making per hour carrying boxes?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Forget that blue toothbrush handle! Can't afford to waste our time here!

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Hey, wait for me!

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Wait, your gem—

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: I was going to say I could offer fifty thousand dinars for it...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Meow...

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Mio? You're back early.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Dejected) Meow...

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: ...It's okay, you tried. It's not easy to see him, is it?

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Hey, Mio, try this.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Touches the pale blue gem with a paw)

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Sniffs)

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Purrs excitedly)

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Rolls in ecstasy)

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Glad you like it... what's that? You found your motivation again?

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Alright, then, go with Woof to find the gems.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: They've finally converged upon this city.
